17/07/26

Maybe, Just Maybe It's the Beginning:

Demand for semiconductors used in AI applications will collapse. The question is not if, but when.

From my perspective there are two most likely scenarios. First: the cost of AI compute rises to a point where demand for AI applications themselves declines, and semiconductor demand collapses as a result. Second: AI reaches a level of power that triggers regulatory intervention or an outright ban, causing demand for AI and therefore for semiconductors to collapse.

What matters is the mechanism behind it. Compute itself can hardly exist in surplus in this sector. AI models are almost infinitely scalable, and more compute simply produces more capable systems. A natural saturation point on the demand side effectively does not exist. The limiting factor is not the need itself, but the capital available to finance it.

This is precisely where the actual risk lies. A classic overproduction, where too many semiconductors are built for a saturated market, I consider highly unlikely. What is realistic instead is overinvestment relative to the ability to pay: capacity is built on the basis of expected revenues that do not yet exist. If the financing disappears or the deployment no longer pays off, demand collapses, even though the technical need would theoretically still be there.

This is where the fundamental difference to the dotcom bubble lies. That bubble was able to fail on its own terms, through overcapacity, missing business models and unfulfilled promises. The current bubble structurally cannot. It requires a concrete external break, close to one of the two scenarios described above.

As long as AI remains available, functional and economically financeable, demand will not dry up on its own. For that reason I consider the comparison to the dotcom bubble structurally inaccurate. These are two fundamentally different cycles whose endpoints rest on entirely different mechanisms.

(Disclaimer: This reflects personal analysis based on publicly available data. This is not financial advice or a recommendation to buy or sell any asset.)
